surface: Current Codex desktop chat using installed ChatNoir skill/helper; source review is performed by the agent

target.name: Roadster Reference
target.kind: Static Python-built web app with browser JavaScript; no identified backend or public content-submission endpoint
target.git_dirty_reason: not checked: Git clean/process filters are configured
target.unchanged_verification: Initial and final included-file hashes and snapshot digest match

baseline.limit: Five heuristic rule families; JS/TS check is lexical only

dismissals.title: HTML/script injection through rendered content
counterevidence: Actual inline renderer emitted no img/script tags for raw HTML.
Actual full builder with synthetic script-closing claim data emitted only the two intended script tags; original text round-tripped through JSON.

dismissals.title: Active-link scheme or attribute injection
counterevidence: Actual destination function rewrote javascript (including mixed case) and data links to #.
An HTTPS URL containing quotes remained one href attribute with no event handler.
Actual validator rejected injected javascript source data; original source data passed.

dismissals.title: Filesystem path escape through Markdown link destinations
counterevidence: The actual destination function raised ValueError for a path outside ROOT.

dismissals.title: Server-side request forgery through source URLs
counterevidence: No server-side URL-fetch operation or deployed backend entrypoint was identified in the reviewed source.

agent_review.scope: Renderer output, source URLs, local path handling and app execution boundaries

controls.observation: img and script input escaped as text; no element tags emitted
javascript (including mixed case) and data schemes rewritten to #
quoted URL remains one href attribute; no event attribute; legitimate HTTPS link preserved
resolved path outside repository rejected by relative_to before use
actual validator rejects injected javascript source URL; original data validates
full actual builder on a synthetic-content scratch copy keeps script-closing text inside JSON; only the two intended script elements emitted

limitations: Source review and local Python/output-parser controls only; no browser execution or live production test.
Repository JSON, Markdown and templates are maintainer-controlled inputs; no public submission endpoint or runtime backend was identified.
No independent dependency-advisory or secret-content scan; all Python runtime imports used here were standard-library or inspected local modules.
No blind or independent evaluation; no security certification or established detection rate.
The lack of a security policy is a documentation gap, not a vulnerability.
Git dirty state is unknown because effective clean/process filters are configured; included-file bytes were verified separately.
Synthetic inputs challenge real rendering functions; they are negative controls, not newly discovered vulnerabilities.
No production requests, package installation, paid model inference or database calls.
